Subject: Data retention & deletion SLAs — follow-up from demo

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. A couple of items came up on our side that we'd need clarified before we move to procurement:

1) SOC 2 status and timeline: are you currently SOC 2 Type II? If not, what is the expected compliance roadmap and controls coverage relevant to logs/backups?

2) Data retention and deletion SLA: what is the standard SLA for customer data deletion requests (including user-level erasures)? How do you handle copies in backups/snapshots?

3) Log retention scope: for audit/debugging logs (request traces, error logs, access logs), what default retention do you offer and can it be customized per-account? Also are any logs retained longer in backups or for compliance reasons?

4) HIPAA/GDPR considerations: for PHI and EU data, are there different retention defaults or contractual options?

I'm attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire (attached) — please confirm who on your side will own returning that and an estimated turnaround. Ideally we can get initial answers this week so procurement can push a draft PO next week.

Jamie — great questions and really helpful prioritization. High level answers below and I copied Monica (CS) and Rishi (security) to own details and the questionnaire return. Below are our immediate replies plus proposed next steps.

High level answers:
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type I with an active Type II audit in progress (expected completion Q3 2026). We can provide the Type I report now and commit to sharing the Type II once available.
- Deletion SLA: standard deletion request for active data is within 72 hours (we confirm logical deletion and start purge processes). Backups/snapshots are retained separately (see details below) and full removal from offline backups can be asynchronous — we provide estimated windows depending on snapshot schedule.
- Log retention: default request/access logs retained 90 days; this is configurable per-account for enterprise customers (we support 30/90/365 day presets).
- HIPAA/GDPR: we have contractual options for extended retention/longer deletion windows and data residency; HIPAA customers typically opt for 180-day snapshot retention unless we agree to different contractual terms.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi will attach a short table clarifying retention windows for: request logs, access logs, KV caches, model outputs, backups/snapshots, and deletion workflow.
2) Monica will own the questionnaire return and coordinate with your procurement on PO timing.
3) We can schedule a 30-min call with security (Rishi + infra lead) tomorrow to walk any technical specifics.

If that works, Monica — can you take the questionnaire as next action? Rishi — can you add the retention table? Jamie — I can set the call and include procurement.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical breakdown so HealthWave has something concrete to feed to legal/procurement. Attaching a compact CSV with the same rows (redwood-retention-clarity-table.csv). Key points below (please reference the attachment for exact fields):

Retention & deletion behavior (defaults):
- Request/Access logs: default 90 days. Configurable to 30/365 for enterprise. Logs are stored encrypted at rest and accessible via console/API.
- Model outputs (generated text): default 30 days for transient inference outputs; can be retained longer per contract.
- KV cache / session cache: ephemeral by default — TTL is 24 hours but can be disabled or shortened.
- Backups / snapshots: incremental snapshots retained for 30 days by default. Snapshots are immutable — deletion from snapshot store is processed asynchronously as part of weekly housekeeping.
- Deletion SLA (logical purge): 72 hours after verified request for active datasets. Physical removal from backups: estimated 30–60 days dependent on snapshot chain and storage provider. We provide attestation of deletion workflows for Type II reports.

HIPAA/GDPR specifics and options:
- HIPAA: we can extend snapshot retention to 180 days if required by operational practice; we also enable customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and dedicated routing for private deployments.
- GDPR Data Subject Erasures: we support account-level erasure workflows and can provide an erase report. For data in snapshots, we provide documented timelines and assist with risk/mitigation language; contractual SLA can specify shorter snapshot retention if needed.

Other notes on backups and compliance:
- Backups are encrypted with AES-256 and stored in region-aligned buckets; access is audited.
- For emergency restore scenarios we maintain a 14-day immutable checkpoint window by default; this is part of our recovery SLAs.
- We do not retain raw PII in logs beyond what is necessary for request tracing; where required, we support field-level redaction and tokenization.

Next action items (technical):
- Ben: confirm whether HealthWave needs a shortened snapshot purge SLA in contract language (e.g., 30 days).
- Monica: take the questionnaire and we'll provide the CSV + SOC I now and Type II when available.
- Jamie/Procurement: flag any contractual language that requires faster physical backup purges — that will determine whether we need legal approval for an exception.

Attachment: redwood-retention-clarity-table.csv

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
